Julia —

Thanks for the quick note and logs. We see matching traces on our side indicating increased end-to-end token latency for the streaming endpoint serving your routing policy between ~08:45–10:30 PST.

Immediate mitigation steps you can apply now (low-risk, no deploy required):
- Disable client-side streaming and fall back to non-streaming generation for critical flows (reduces sensitivity to bursty token arrival).
- Reduce max_tokens to 256 for high-concurrency clients and set response_timeout to 45s to avoid UI lockups.
- If you use prefix caching, set cache_ttl to 30m to improve prefix hit rate during retries.
- Toggle request-level routing to prefer region-us-east-1 until the west-coast shard recovers (we'll provide a temporary routing tag).

I'll loop in our SRE and product teams. Ben/Marissa — please see logs and confirm we are routing HearthPay to alternate shards and whether an immediate capacity bump is needed.

— Soojin

We triaged the shard group serving region-us-west-2 that hosts HearthPay's streaming instances. Summary: degraded KV cache hit rates + an in-flight cache-eviction loop caused intermittent stalls in the token pumping pipeline. Root cause appears to be a combination of a new cache eviction heuristic (rolled to a subset of shards in last week's rollout) and a concurrent large-batch warmup from another tenant that saturated the async I/O queue.

Short-term actions (already executed):
- Shifted HearthPay traffic to warm standby shards in us-east-1 (completed at 09:50 PST).
- Applied a conservative cache-eviction override to affected shards to prevent the eviction loop.
- Increased the async I/O worker pool by 30% on the impacted hosts.

Expected impact: token flow should stabilize within 10–20 minutes after the shift; we will monitor for regressions until 12:00 PST.

Longer-term fixes planned:
- Revert the heuristic change and implement a controlled RB rollout with improved telemetry (targeted for next maintenance window, 2027-05-25).
- Add backpressure safeguards in the batch warmup path and better tenant isolation for async I/O.

I will update this thread when we have full confirmation.

— Karthik (SRE)

Hi Julia —

Quick update and formal postmortem summary:

What happened:
- Between ~08:45–10:30 PST on 2027-05-21, HearthPay experienced elevated token latency on the streaming endpoint due to a cache-eviction loop on west-coast shards compounded by a high-volume batch warmup from another tenant. This caused token emission to pause in short bursts (10–25s).

Impact:
- ~12% of HearthPay realtime sessions experienced degraded UX or client timeouts during the window. No customer data or requests were lost; all requests were processed after routing to standby shards.

Immediate mitigations taken by Redwood:
- Traffic rerouted to warm standby shards in us-east-1 at 09:50 PST.
- Eviction heuristic override and async I/O worker increase applied to affected hosts.
- We provided HearthPay short-term client recommendations (non-streaming fallback, lower max_tokens, routing tag).

Committed next steps:
- Revert the eviction heuristic and re-roll with additional telemetry (planned 2027-05-25).
- Implement async I/O tenant isolation and rate-capping in the warmup path (ETA 3 weeks).
- Provide HearthPay with a credit for impacted usage during the incident window; Ben will follow up on commercial terms.

Attachments and links: logs we referenced (client-logs-20270521.txt, heap-snapshot-05-21.json) and the internal incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-2312. Postmortem doc: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/ops/hearthpay/20270521-postmortem.md
